criteria.description: Fidelity to body: Verify each claim sentence-by-sentence against the body. Defects include invented or misattributed facts, merging results from different objects (e.g., zeta Gem vs eta Aql), upgrading ongoing/future VLTI work to completed results, adding numeric ranges not present in body, and omitting caveats the body states. Several such defects should cap this criterion at 6 or below.

Coverage of problem, method, and findings: Abstract must state the calibration problem for the Cepheid P-L relation, the geometric Baade-Wesselink method requiring interferometric diameters, and findings supported by body: phase- and wavelength-dependent limb darkening from time-dependent non-LTE hydrodynamic models, shape change not just amount, few-percent corrections in optical and ~2% level in near-IR/K-band, and VLTI/AMBER capability. Vague generic abstracts with no findings score low; detail counts only when accurate.

Uncertainty, structure, and length: Abstract must preserve appropriate uncertainty (feasibility, future potential, not claimed completed calibration), have coherent abstract structure (~89 words), and not invent citations. Enforce requested length: exceeding target by >~30% must lose points on this criterion scaled to overshoot. Copying source tokenization spacing is only a minor presentation issue, not a content error.
